# poke-engine gen3 patch set — SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the patch list and its order.
#
# Read by BOTH builders:
#   scripts/vendor_poke_engine_src.sh — vendors the Rust source into
#     third_party/poke-engine-src/ for the native pokezero-search crate.
#   scripts/setup_poke_engine.sh      — builds the Python wheel that the
#     wheel-driven harnesses import (pokezero.engine_fidelity,
#     scripts/engine_fidelity_multiturn.py, scripts/rapidspin_differential.py).
#
# They used to carry separate hand-maintained lists and DID drift: the wheel
# builder sat on the first five patches while the vendored source grew to eight,
# so every wheel-driven harness was silently measuring an older gen3 engine than
# the one the search crate links. Add a patch HERE and both builders pick it up.
#
# Format: one patch filename per line, relative to third_party/, in APPLY ORDER.
# Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. Order is load-bearing — each patch is
# authored against the tree the ones above it leave behind — and both builders
# apply with `--fuzz=0`, so a version bump fails loudly instead of applying hunks
# at shifted locations.
#
# Rationale for each fix lives in docs/engine_fidelity_findings.md; the summaries
# below say what the patch touches and what it is authored against.

# gen3 end-of-turn residual order: Leftovers (5) + Shed Skin (5.3), then Leech
# Seed (8), then poison/toxic/burn damage (9/10), then threshold berries + Rain
# Dish + Speed Boost (10+). Upstream ran ALL items/abilities after status damage,
# netting residuals against the Leftovers heal.
poke-engine-gen3-residual-order.patch

# gen3 Attract (infatuation) 50%-per-turn move immobilization. Upstream accepts
# the ATTRACT volatile but wholly ignores it (zero behavioral references in
# gen3); adds the 50/50 chance branch mirroring the confusion self-hit so search
# prices it. Authored against the residual-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-attract.patch

# gen3 Struggle is TYPELESS (neutral vs all types incl. Ghost, no STAB), per real
# Gen II+ mechanics; upstream defines Struggle as Normal-type, which wrongly made
# gen3 Struggle immune vs Ghost and resisted by Rock/Steel. Compile-time gated so
# gen1 stays Normal. Authored against the attract-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-struggle-typeless.patch

# gen3 Rapid Spin / Protect fidelity. (1) Protect leak: the move-id-keyed
# post-hit handlers (choice_hazard_clear, choice_special_effect) survived
# remove_effects_for_protect() (which leaves move_id intact), so a
# Protect-blocked Rapid Spin still stripped the spinner's own Spikes, and Seismic
# Toss/Super Fang/Endeavor etc. still dealt fixed damage THROUGH Protect.
# before_move now returns a blocked_by_protect bool threaded to those handlers,
# which early-return when blocked (never gated on damage/hit_sub, so a spin that
# connects on a Substitute STILL clears). (2) A connecting Rapid Spin now also
# frees the user from Leech Seed and partial-trapping (Wrap/Bind/Fire Spin/Clamp/
# Whirlpool) — previously unmodelled. Verified vs real gen3 Showdown
# (scripts/rapidspin_differential.py). Touches generate_instructions.rs +
# choice_effects.rs only. Authored against the struggle-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-rapidspin-fidelity.patch

# Full Gen 3 randbats ability audit corrections: exact chance branches and
# status/volatile immunity, recoil/Wonder Guard/Sturdy, Forecast/weather
# suppression, gender-aware Cute Charm, Intimidate through Substitute, Gen 3
# Lightning Rod singles semantics, and speed-tie isolation. Authored against the
# rapidspin-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-ability-fidelity.patch

# gen3 Baton Pass carries the Perish Song counter. Showdown copies every volatile
# without a `noCopy` flag (sim/pokemon.ts copyVolatileFrom) and the perish
# volatiles carry none in gen3 (which inherits gen4 -> gen5; neither mod
# overrides them), so the count rides the pass and the RECEIVER faints at
# perish0. Upstream's remove_volatile_statuses_on_switch retained only Substitute
# and Leech Seed, so the engine believed Baton Pass escapes Perish Song. Verified
# vs real gen3 Showdown (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_switch_fidelity.rs. Touches gen3/state.rs only.
poke-engine-gen3-batonpass-perish.patch

# gen3 Spikes deal 1/8, 1/6 and 1/4 of max HP at one, two and three layers.
# Showdown computes `[0, 3, 4, 6][layers] * maxhp / 24` (data/mods/gen4/moves.ts,
# inherited by gen3 — gen3 -> gen4, NOT gen5) and rounds through
# `clampIntRange(damage, 1)`: floor, minimum 1 HP. Upstream used
# `maxhp * layers / 8`, which over-damages by exactly 1.5x at two and three
# layers and dealt ZERO to a 1 HP Shedinja. Verified vs real gen3 Showdown
# (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py: spikes2layers/spikes3layers); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_hazard_residual_fidelity.rs. Touches the switch
# routine in gen3/generate_instructions.rs only.
poke-engine-gen3-spikes-layers.patch

# gen3 resolves a forced replacement BEFORE the end-of-turn residual block.
# Showdown's runAction sees the pending switch flag, issues a `switch` request
# and returns with the queued `residual` action untouched, so the block runs only
# once the replacement is on the field — and applies to the replacement too.
# Upstream ran the residuals in the same instruction set as the faint (and, for a
# slow pivot, dropped them entirely), so an incoming Pokemon never took sand/hail/
# status damage on the turn it came in and the weather/screen counters ticked on
# the wrong side of the switch. The deferral is marked with the existing per-side
# `force_switch` flag via its existing reversible toggle instruction, which is
# what keeps a faint caused BY the residual block — already run — from being
# mistaken for a pending one and double-applying. Verified vs real gen3 Showdown
# (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py: faintresiduals + control); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_hazard_residual_fidelity.rs. Touches the
# end-of-turn generation in gen3/generate_instructions.rs plus get_all_options in
# gen3/state.rs. Authored against the spikes-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-residual-defer-on-faint.patch

# gen3 CONFUSION is a BOUNDED stochastic duration, and Baton Pass carries it.
# Upstream modelled confusion as permanent until switch-out (no expiry path
# anywhere in src/gen3/), so search saw an unbounded 50%-per-turn self-hit.
# Showdown rolls `time = this.random(2, 6)` once at addVolatile
# (data/conditions.ts `confusion.onStart`, which gen3 inherits) and gen3's
# onBeforeMove (the gen4 mod's) decrements first, snaps out and lets the move
# through at zero, and only otherwise rolls the 50% self-hit — so a self-hit roll
# happens on `time - 1` attacking turns, uniform on {1,2,3,4}. Modelled as the
# same hazard ladder gen3 sleep already uses (`chance_confusion_ends`, mirroring
# `chance_to_wake_up`) over the ALREADY-PRESENT
# `volatile_status_durations.confusion` counter, forked at end of turn where both
# outcomes are terminal. Also (a) moves the full-paralysis roll after the
# confusion and Attract branches to match Showdown's onBeforeMove priorities
# (confusion 3 > attract 2 > par 1), which the counter needs to advance on a
# fully-paralyzed turn, and (b) retains CONFUSION with its counter across a Baton
# Pass (`copyVolatileFrom` shallow-clones every volatile lacking `noCopy`;
# confusion has none in gen3's chain) — deliberately deferred by the
# batonpass-perish patch, since carrying a PERMANENT confusion would have been
# worse than dropping it. Verified vs real gen3 Showdown
# (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_confusion_fidelity.rs. Touches
# gen3/generate_instructions.rs, gen3/state.rs and gen3/abilities.rs. Shares the
# end-of-turn branch site with residual-defer-on-faint (the confusion ladder
# forks each branch right where Shed Skin does), so it is authored against the
# residual-defer-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-confusion-duration.patch

# gen3 Transform (Ditto / Mew) implemented in rollouts. Upstream defines
# Choices::TRANSFORM in the MOVES table and NOWHERE else — no effect arm in any
# generation, no tests — so clicking Transform changed nothing at all, which is
# why it dominated the engine-search world-construction failure census. Copies
# species, the target's CURRENT types, the five non-HP stats, all seven boosts,
# the target's ability (`gen > 2` — a Ditto that copies Flygon is `-immune` to
# Earthquake) and the moveset at Math.min(5, move.pp) = 5 PP per slot; copies
# neither HP nor status; fails only against an already-transformed target (gen3
# lets it bypass Substitute, and Protect does not block it); reverts on
# switch-out. Expressed entirely through the instruction system — FormeChange,
# ChangeType (plus the TYPECHANGE volatile, whose switch-out arm already restores
# types -> base_types), the five stat deltas, Boost, ChangeAbility — plus two NEW
# instructions, ChangeMoveId (upstream had no reversible move-slot instruction at
# all) and ChangeTransformSnapshot, backed by a new Pokemon::pre_transform record
# of the transformer's base form, so every mutation inverts exactly and
# size_of::<Instruction>() stays 6. Deliberate approximations (weight not copied
# — its only gen3 consumer is Low Kick, absent from all 393 gen3 randbats sets
# across the pool's 220 species;
# max PP not modelled — the engine has no such field) are spelled out in the
# patch header. Verified vs real gen3 Showdown
# (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py: transform + 4 more); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_transform_fidelity.rs. Touches src/instruction.rs,
# src/state.rs, gen3/state.rs, gen3/choice_effects.rs and poke-engine-py/src/lib.rs.
# Authored against the confusion-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-transform.patch

# State serialization must be a fixed point. Side::serialize writes the volatile
# set with a TRAILING ":" and Side::deserialize split on ":" without discarding
# the empty tail; PokemonVolatileStatus::from_str("") does not fail (the
# define_enum_with_from_str! macro declares `default = NONE`), so every state
# carrying a volatile silently gained a NONE and re-serializing emitted it back.
# State::deserialize is how pokezero_search receives its root world, so this made
# search read a different state than the caller built, and the phantom volatile
# reached the instruction stream as a RemoveVolatileStatus(NONE) on every
# switch-out. Fixed on the READER, so the wire format is unchanged and every
# previously written state string still parses. Pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_state_roundtrip.rs. Touches src/state.rs only;
# authored against the transform-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-state-roundtrip.patch

# gen3 move-trapping: Mean Look, Spider Web and Block. All three resolve to
# `target.addVolatile('trapped', source, move, 'trapper')` in Showdown, leaving
# the victim with `trapped: true` and NO switch options until the trapper leaves
# the field. Upstream defined all three as pure no-ops (no volatile_status, no
# effect anywhere in src/), so the engine believed they did nothing — which made
# every real Mean Look / Spider Web turn unrepresentable to the search world and
# fell the whole root back to a non-search choice. Both are in the gen3 randbats
# pool (Misdreavus / Ariados); Block is not, and rides along only because it is
# literally the same Showdown handler.
#
# Semantics pinned against the real sim (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py:
# meanlook / spiderweb / meanlookprotect / meanlooksub / meanlooktrapperleaves /
# meanlookbatonpass): the trap has no duration and no residual; Ghost types are
# NOT exempt (the trapping immunity arrives in gen6 — gen5's typechart override
# drops the `trapped: 3` entry gen3 would otherwise inherit); Protect blocks it
# (gen3 inherits the gen5 mod's protect flag on Mean Look and Block); a
# Substitute blocks it (no bypasssub — the sim answers `-fail`); the volatile is
# LINKED, so an ordinary switch-out by the trapper, or its faint, frees the
# victim; and gen3/4 alone re-declare BOTH `trapped` and `trapper` with
# `noCopy: false`, which makes Baton Pass carry the trap in either direction.
#
# The Baton Pass asymmetry is the subtle part and is pinned from both ends. The
# VICTIM passing carries its own trap to the receiver. The TRAPPER passing does
# NOT release the victim: `copyVolatileFrom` copies `trapper` to the receiver,
# DELETES the old trapper's linkedPokemon/linkedStatus, and only then runs
# `clearVolatile()` — which finds no link left to release — while the victim's
# link is re-pointed to the receiver. So the trap changes OWNER, and the
# RECEIVER's later departure is what frees the victim. This is the line the pool
# is built around: 2 of the 3 gen3 randbats Ariados sets carry Spider Web AND
# Baton Pass. The release is therefore gated on the switching side not
# baton-passing; the pre-existing PARTIALLYTRAPPED release next to it is
# deliberately left unconditional, because Wrap/Fire Spin is not a linked
# volatile at all — `partiallytrapped.onResidual` releases on `!source.isActive`,
# which holds however the source left the field.
#
# Adds a TRAPPED variant to the gen3 volatile enum (distinct from
# PARTIALLYTRAPPED, the Wrap/Fire Spin residual family) and applies it from
# gen3/choice_effects.rs rather than as a declarative volatile_status on the
# Choice, because the MOVES table in src/choices.rs is shared by all four
# compiled generations and only gen3 gains the variant. The one shared-file edit
# is the gen3-gated protect flag, in the same `cfg!(feature = ...)` style the
# struggle-typeless patch already uses. Pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_trap_perish_fidelity.rs. Touches
# gen3/state.rs, gen3/choice_effects.rs, gen3/generate_instructions.rs and
# choices.rs; authored against the confusion-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-move-trapping.patch

# `get_all_options` must never return an EMPTY option vector: MCTS indexes
# straight into it (`Node::maximize_ucb_for_side` returns index 0 for an empty
# slice, `Node::expand` then panics "index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the
# index is 0" and the whole search dies). Every exit guards `len() == 0` except
# the two `force_switch` branches, which call `add_move_from_choice` — a no-op
# when the saved move is absent from the current active's slots — and return
# early, skipping the guard. So a side owing a forced replacement while the other
# side carries a `switch_out_move_second_saved_move` its active does not know
# handed back `[]`. Reachable because engine_world samples a pending Baton Pass
# commitment into that field; only ever fired on INTERIOR tree nodes, because
# root_get_all_options already guards its own exits. An unsatisfiable commitment
# means NO ACTION this boundary, not NO OPTION, so those branches now fall back to
# MoveChoice::None like every other exit. Pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_terminal_options.rs. Touches the two
# force_switch branches of gen3/state.rs only; authored against the
# move-trapping-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-terminal-options.patch

# gen3 ENCORE is a BOUNDED duration, and upstream never expires it in gen3. The
# `volatile_status_durations.encore` counter exists and is serialized, but the
# only code that advances it is `#[cfg]`-gated to gen5+, so a gen3 Encore locks
# its victim for the rest of the battle. Confirmed by the differential lane
# (D9, seeds 991000-991059: 3/4/5/6-turn ends observed across 60 samples).
#
# gen3 overrides the duration EXPLICITLY: data/mods/gen3/moves.ts gives
# `encore.condition.durationCallback() { return this.random(3, 7); }`, uniform on
# {3,4,5,6}. This is the gen3-inherits-gen4-NOT-gen5 trap in its sharpest form —
# gen4's own override says `this.random(4, 9)` = {4..8}, and gen5-gen8 do not
# define encore at all, so taking any neighbour's value gives the wrong window.
#
# Unlike confusion this is Showdown's GENERIC duration machinery, not an
# onBeforeMove counter: sim/battle.ts decrements `handler.state.duration` once
# per turn in the RESIDUAL phase and calls `end` at zero, so the tick lands
# whether or not the encored Pokemon moved — and the engine's end-of-turn block
# is that same point in the turn, not an approximation of one. Modelled as the
# same hazard ladder confusion and sleep already use (`chance_encore_ends`):
# 0 while n < 3, then 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, forced, which multiplies out to a uniform
# 1/4 per outcome with nothing surviving a seventh tick (derivation in the
# function's header). Also models `onStart`'s
# `if (!queue.willMove(target)) duration++` compensation — seeding the counter at
# -1 when the encorer moved second — which is what makes the victim locked for
# exactly `duration` turns regardless of speed order, and the `onResidual` early
# termination when the encored move hits 0 PP. Encore carries `noCopy: true`, so
# unlike confusion it is NOT carried by Baton Pass; the switch-out arm drops it
# and zeroes the counter. Verified vs real gen3 Showdown
# (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_encore_fidelity.rs. Touches
# gen3/generate_instructions.rs and gen3/state.rs; authored against the
# terminal-options-patched tree, applied last of the BEHAVIOUR patches.
poke-engine-gen3-encore-duration.patch


# gen3 Encore's APPLICATION-failure set. The duration patch above bounded how
# long an Encore lasts; this one bounds when it may start at all. Upstream asked
# only whether the target had ever used a move, so the engine would happily
# Encore a Struggle — Showdown's `encore.condition.onStart` also refuses on the
# move's identity and on its PP:
#
#     let move = target.lastMove;
#     if (!move || target.volatiles['dynamax']) return false;
#     const moveSlot = target.getMoveData(move.id);
#     if (move.isZ || move.isMax || move.flags['failencore'] ||
#         !moveSlot || moveSlot.pp <= 0) return false;
#
# `dynamax`/`isZ`/`isMax` are unreachable in gen3. `!moveSlot` is structurally
# unreachable in the engine, which stores last_used_move as a SLOT INDEX rather
# than a move id, so it always denotes a real slot; the case it exists to catch
# in Showdown is Struggle, which is not in `moveSlots` and which the flag list
# below rejects anyway. The two already-handled arms stay right: LastUsedMove
# ::None is `!move`, and ::Switch is a fresh switch-in — `Pokemon.clearVolatile()`
# nulls `lastMove` on switch-out (sim/pokemon.ts), so Encore genuinely fails
# against a Pokemon that just came in.
#
# The `failencore` set had to be resolved against gen3's ACTUAL mod chain
# (gen3 -> gen4 -> gen5 -> gen6 -> gen7 -> gen8 -> base data/moves.ts),
# remembering that a mod's `flags` object REPLACES its parent's wholesale rather
# than merging into it. Six moves carry it as gen3 sees them:
#
#     mimic, mirrormove, sketch, struggle   flags from data/mods/gen3/moves.ts
#     encore, transform                     flags from data/mods/gen4/moves.ts
#
# The replacement rule cuts BOTH ways, and the inverse cases are the trap. Four
# more moves carry `failencore` in base data/moves.ts but LOSE it to a nearer
# override that re-declares flags without it:
#
#     assist        gen3  { metronome, noassist, nosleeptalk }
#     metronome     gen4  { noassist, failcopycat, nosleeptalk, failmimic }
#     naturepower   gen4  { metronome }
#     sleeptalk     gen6  { nosleeptalk, noassist, failcopycat }
#
# so none of the four fails Encore in gen3 and none belongs in the list. Reading
# base — or gen8, which re-adds the flag to sleeptalk and mirrormove — would
# over-fail all four.
#
# The hardcoded six are therefore DELIBERATE, and regenerating this list
# programmatically needs care: a Dex-derived set for gen3 resolves TWELVE moves,
# because six more leak in from the inherited base table with no gen3-legal
# existence at all — blazingtorque, combattorque, dynamaxcannon, magicaltorque,
# noxioustorque and wickedtorque, all gen8/gen9. Anyone re-deriving this must
# intersect against the gen3 move pool as well as walking the flag overrides.
#
# Coupled with poke-engine-gen3-lastmove-semantics.patch below: this patch
# decides Encore's fate FROM `last_used_move`, so a wrong last_used_move makes a
# right failure set produce the wrong answer. The two are one story — the
# application gate and the value it reads — and should be reviewed and changed
# together. Verified vs real gen3 Showdown
# (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_encore_failencore_fidelity.rs. Touches the
# Encore arm of move_has_no_effect in gen3/generate_instructions.rs only;
# authored against the encore-duration-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-encore-failencore.patch

# gen3 residual ROUNDING ORDER, the toxic ladder and the weather minimum.
#
# (1) Toxic. Showdown's `tox` residual is
#       this.damage(this.clampIntRange(pokemon.baseMaxhp / 16, 1) * stage)
# (data/conditions.ts; gen3 inherits gen4's `tox`, which only re-orders the
# residual and inherits this body): the per-stage tick is FLOORED and clamped to
# a minimum of 1 FIRST, and only then multiplied by the stage counter. Upstream
# computed floor(maxhp * stage / 16) — flooring AFTER the multiply. Writing
# maxhp = 16q + r, Showdown deals q*stage while upstream deals
# q*stage + floor(r*stage/16), so the two agree only when maxhp is a multiple of
# 16 and the engine otherwise OVER-damages by up to stage-1 HP, widening every
# turn the ladder climbs. This was 55% of the strict-matcher residue against the
# real sim. Verified: a 651 max HP Blissey (651 % 16 == 11, floor(651/16) == 40)
# ticks 40/80/120/160/200 in the sim, where upstream dealt 40/81/122/162/203.
#
# (2) Hail and sandstorm. `onWeather` is `this.damage(target.baseMaxhp / 16)`,
# and every damage() call runs through `clampIntRange(damage, 1)` in
# spreadDamage — floor, then a hard floor of 1 HP. Upstream truncated
# `maxhp * 0.0625` with no clamp, so anything under 16 max HP took ZERO chip
# damage forever. Shedinja (1 max HP) is in the gen3 randbats pool and the real
# sim kills it with sand/hail.
#
# Burn and poison were checked in the same sweep and are CORRECT: gen3 inherits
# gen6's brn override (baseMaxhp / 8, not the modern /16) and the base psn
# (baseMaxhp / 8), both of which upstream already matches, and both already carry
# the minimum-1 clamp. Neither has a stage multiplier, so neither can express the
# rounding-order bug. Pinned so that stays true.
#
# Verified vs real gen3 Showdown (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py:
# toxicladder + toxicladdercontrol + sandminimum); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_residual_rounding_fidelity.rs. Touches the
# end-of-turn block in gen3/generate_instructions.rs only; authored against the
# encore-patched tree, applied before the fixture refresh.
poke-engine-gen3-residual-rounding.patch
# gen3 `last_used_move` is recorded only for a move that ACTUALLY EXECUTED.
# Showdown sets `lastMove` in `Pokemon.moveUsed()`, called from
# `BattleActions.runMove` (sim/battle-actions.ts:291) at exactly one point —
# after the `BeforeMove` gate has passed and after PP has been deducted:
#
#     const willTryMove = this.battle.runEvent('BeforeMove', ...);
#     if (!willTryMove) { runEvent('MoveAborted', ...); ...; return; }
#     if (move.beforeMoveCallback) { ... return; }
#     if (!pokemon.deductPP(...) && move.id !== 'struggle') { 'cant nopp'; return; }
#     pokemon.moveUsed(move, targetLoc);            // <- lastMove set here
#
# Every immobilizer sits behind that gate by returning false from its
# onBeforeMove — full paralysis (gen4 par), sleep (gen3 slp), freeze (gen4 frz),
# flinch, a confusion self-hit (gen4 confusion), infatuation — so none of them
# records a last move. The engine recorded it BEFORE
# generate_instructions_from_existing_status_conditions, so a fully-paralyzed or
# self-hitting turn still counted as "used". That is not cosmetic: Encore's
# onStart reads lastMove, so the engine could Encore a move the target never got
# to make, and (since the failencore patch above) decide Encore's fate from it.
#
# The fix moves the record point below that call and below the still-asleep early
# return, so only the branch on which the move really executes reaches it. It
# stays ABOVE move_has_no_effect and the accuracy roll on purpose: moveUsed
# precedes useMove, so a move that misses, fails outright, or is blocked by
# Protect still counts as used.
#
# Sleep Talk needed explicit handling rather than riding the move: it is
# `sleepUsable`, so gen3's slp.onBeforeMove returns undefined and Sleep Talk
# itself reaches moveUsed, while the move it CALLS goes through useMove, which
# never touches lastMove. So the caller records and the called move must not —
# a naive relocation would have inverted exactly that. Pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_lastmove_semantics.rs (a row per truth-table
# entry, including the confusion/paralysis composition from the confusion patch).
# Touches generate_instructions_from_move in gen3/generate_instructions.rs only;
# authored against the failencore-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-lastmove-semantics.patch
# gen3 phazing is blocked by Protect. Whirlwind and Roar inherit gen4's flag
# override (data/mods/gen4/moves.ts):
#     flags: { protect: 1, mirror: 1, bypasssub: 1, metronome: 1 }
# so in gen3 a phaze IS stopped by Protect, goes THROUGH a Substitute, and is NOT
# bounced by Magic Coat (reflectable arrives with gen5's override). Upstream
# carried no protect flag on either move, so `before_move` never reached
# `remove_effects_for_protect()` — which is what clears `flags.drag` — and the
# target was dragged out through its own Protect. Verified against the real sim:
# Whirlwind into Protect answers `-activate <target> Protect` with no `|drag|`.
#
# Reachable and common: Protect is on 43 of the gen3 randbats species, and the
# pool's own Whirlwind user (Skarmory) carries Protect AND Whirlwind on the same
# set. Roar is carried by Blastoise and Steelix.
#
# Scope, deliberately: the `reflectable: true` upstream puts on both moves is
# WRONG for gen3, but is left alone because gen3 models no reflect/Magic Coat
# path at all (the flag is inert) and Magic Coat appears on 0 of 393 gen3
# randbats sets (220 species). Gen 3 Ingrain also blocks phazing (sim-verified)
# and is likewise not modelled — Ingrain is on 0 of 393 sets too, so it is
# unreachable in this format.
#
# Everything else in the phaze path was verified CORRECT while chasing this and
# is pinned rather than changed: the fan-out is uniform over the target's alive,
# non-active reserve (Showdown's `this.sample(possibleSwitches)`), the dragged-in
# Pokemon eats entry hazards, the outgoing Pokemon's boosts are cleared, a
# Substitute does not block, and a phaze with no living reserve is a no-op.
#
# Verified vs real gen3 Showdown (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py:
# whirlwindprotect / roarprotect / whirlwinddrag / whirlwindspikes); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_phaze_fidelity.rs. Touches two flag literals in
# the shared src/choices.rs, both gen3-gated in the same `cfg!(feature = ...)`
# style as the struggle-typeless and move-trapping patches; authored against the
# residual-rounding tree, applied before the fixture refresh.
poke-engine-gen3-phaze-protect.patch
# gen3 variable base power: Flail and Reversal.
#
# Both moves share one ladder and gen3 declares its OWN callback for EACH of
# them — data/mods/gen3/moves.ts:273 (flail) and :496 (reversal), verified
# independently rather than assumed from one another:
#
#     const ratio = Math.max(Math.floor(pokemon.hp * 48 / pokemon.maxhp), 1);
#     ratio < 2  -> 200      ratio < 17 -> 80
#     ratio < 5  -> 150      ratio < 33 -> 40
#     ratio < 10 -> 100      else       -> 20
#
# THE INHERITANCE TRAP HAS THREE DIRECTIONS and this patch set has now been bitten
# by all three; check every one before trusting a rule:
#   1. inherit-from-gen4       — gen3 Spikes takes gen4's layer fractions
#                                (poke-engine-gen3-spikes-layers.patch);
#   2. inherit-from-further-up — gen3 burn takes GEN6's baseMaxhp/8, not the
#                                modern /16 (poke-engine-gen3-residual-rounding.patch);
#   3. gen3-overrides-everything — THIS patch: gen3 re-declares the move itself,
#                                so no ancestor's table applies at all.
# Read gen3's own mod file first; walk up only from where it is silent.
#
# Two upstream bugs, one per move:
#   FLAIL had no arm anywhere in src/gen3/ and no base_power, so it was INERT —
#   literally zero damage at every HP fraction, a missing damage component rather
#   than a wrong value (the same gap shape as Transform).
#   REVERSAL had the ladder written as ROUNDED FLOAT ratios (0.688 / 0.354 /
#   0.208 / 0.104 / 0.042). ALL FIVE breakpoints were misclassified, in two
#   directions — the two outer constants rounded HIGH and the three middle ones
#   LOW — each producing its own distinct wrong band:
#       33/48 = 0.6875    -> 0.688 HIGH : scored  40, sim says  20
#       17/48 = 0.354166  -> 0.354 LOW  : scored  40, sim says  80
#       10/48 = 0.208333  -> 0.208 LOW  : scored  80, sim says 100
#        5/48 = 0.104166  -> 0.104 LOW  : scored 100, sim says 150
#        2/48 = 0.041666  -> 0.042 HIGH : scored 200, sim says 150
#   Reproducing the integer floor exactly removes all five bands, and with them
#   the whole class: an exhaustive (hp, maxhp) sweep across the realistic gen3
#   max-HP range leaves no disagreement.
#
# Gen 4's 64-scale (cut points 2/6/13/22/43) disagrees with gen3's at exactly
# four percentages of max HP — 4%, 10%, 35%, 68% — where gen3 scores
# 200/150/80/40 and gen4 would score 150/100/40/20. Gen 3 is the HIGHER one at
# every divergence, so borrowing gen4's table under-powers both moves in exactly
# the desperation region they exist for. Those four are pinned by name.
#
# Reachability (pool: 220 species / 393 sets): flail 1 set (Dodrio), reversal 8
# sets (Blaziken, Furret, Heracross, Hitmonlee, Medicham, Primeape, ...). The
# rest of the variable-BP family was audited and left alone: eruption and
# waterspout are implemented and correct (base_power * hp/maxhp, no gen3-chain
# override) but appear on 0 of 393 sets; seismic toss (17 sets) is level-based
# and already handled; night shade, super fang, psywave, low kick, magnitude and
# present are all 0 of 393. Return (41 sets) is happiness-based and correctly
# fixed at BP 102: Showdown defaults happiness to 255 when a set omits it
# (sim/pokemon.ts:342), and Return's callback is floor(happiness * 10 / 25), so
# floor(255 * 10 / 25) = 102. The 102 is the BASE POWER, not the happiness.
#
# One more recorded non-difference so nobody re-derives it: Showdown computes
# Eruption/Water Spout as basePower * hp / maxhp (multiply, THEN divide) while
# the engine computes basePower * (hp / maxhp) (divide, then multiply). Those are
# identical in exact arithmetic and can differ by one ULP in f32 — unreachable
# here at 0 of 393 sets, and left alone rather than churned.
#
# Verified vs real gen3 Showdown (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py:
# flailladder / reversalladder / flailladdercontrol); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_variable_bp_fidelity.rs. Touches the
# modify_choice ladder in gen3/choice_effects.rs only; authored against the
# phaze-patched tree, applied before the fixture refresh.
poke-engine-gen3-variable-bp.patch



# gen3 PP is charged only for a move that ACTUALLY EXECUTED. Showdown deducts in
# BattleActions.runMove (sim/battle-actions.ts:282), inside the same
# `if (!externalMove)` block that ends in moveUsed (line 291), and only once the
# BeforeMove gate has passed:
#
#     const willTryMove = this.battle.runEvent('BeforeMove', ...);
#     if (!willTryMove) { ...; return; }              // no PP charged
#     ...
#     if (!pokemon.deductPP(baseMove, null, target) && move.id !== 'struggle') {
#         this.battle.add('cant', pokemon, 'nopp', move); ...; return;
#     }
#     pokemon.moveUsed(move, targetLoc);
#
# So an immobilized turn is FREE -- full paralysis, staying asleep, staying
# frozen, flinching, a confusion self-hit and infatuation all return false from
# their onBeforeMove and never reach the deduction. The engine charged before
# generate_instructions_from_existing_status_conditions, so a paralyzed Pokemon
# burned PP for turns it never acted on.
#
# That phantom drain is load-bearing now that Encore reads PP: encore.onResidual
# ends Encore the moment the locked move hits 0, and encore.onStart refuses a
# target already at 0, so draining PP the sim never spent frees a seat Showdown
# keeps locked. This is the third and last piece of the runMove prologue, after
# lastmove-semantics: the gate order, the record, and the charge now all agree.
#
# Placed immediately ABOVE the last_used_move record that patch installed, since
# Showdown deducts first and records second, and below the still-asleep early
# return so only the branch that really executes reaches it. It stays ABOVE
# move_has_no_effect and the accuracy roll, because the deduction precedes
# useMove -- a move that misses, fails outright or is blocked by Protect still
# pays. `!choice.sleep_talk_move` is Showdown's `if (!externalMove)`: Sleep Talk
# pays for itself and the move it calls never deducts.
#
# Pressure needs no separate placement, and collapsing the two deductions into
# one 1-or-2 decrement is EXACT rather than merely convenient. Being post-gate is
# not sufficient on its own; what makes it exact is that there is NO WINDOW
# between the two sites. Nothing between battle-actions.ts:282 (the base point)
# and :482 (Pressure's extra, via the DeductPP event inside useMove) can abort
# the move -- every abort path in runMove has already returned above :282, and
# useMove's own failure points (TryMove, accuracy, immunity, Protect) all sit
# BELOW :482 -- so the two either both happen or neither does. And neither point
# refunds: a miss or a failed move never gives PP back, which is why both sites
# can be hoisted to a single decrement without changing any observable. If a
# future gen introduced an abort between them, or a refund-on-miss rule, the
# collapse would stop being sound and the two would have to be split again.
#
# NOT fixed here, verified and left for its own change: Showdown skips the
# deduction entirely on a LOCKED continuation turn (`if (!lockedMove)`), while the
# engine charges every turn of an Outrage / Petal Dance / Thrash. Distinct
# observable, needs its own pins. Pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_pp_ordering.rs; touches
# generate_instructions_from_move in gen3/generate_instructions.rs only; authored
# against the phaze-protect-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-pp-ordering.patch
# gen3 LOCKED continuation turns cost no PP. Showdown guards the deduction on
# getLockedMove() (sim/battle-actions.ts:280-283):
#
#     const lockedMove = pokemon.getLockedMove();
#     if (!lockedMove) {
#         if (!pokemon.deductPP(baseMove, null, target) && move.id !== 'struggle') { ... }
#     } else { sourceEffect = this.dex.conditions.get('lockedmove'); }
#
# getLockedMove fires the LockMove priority event, whose providers in gen3's
# chain are the `lockedmove` condition (Outrage / Thrash / Petal Dance,
# data/conditions.ts:282), `twoturnmove` (Solar Beam, Sky Attack, Dig, Fly, Razor
# Wind, Skull Bash, data/conditions.ts:317), `mustrecharge`
# (data/conditions.ts:377), and rollout / bide in data/moves.ts. So a whole lock
# costs ONE PP, charged on the turn that starts it -- which is why Showdown tags
# the second half of a two-turn move `[from] lockedmove`.
#
# REACHABILITY, and why the shape of this fix is not what it first looks like:
# the lockedmove TRIO is absent from the gen3 randbats pool -- 0 carriers each
# for Outrage, Thrash and Petal Dance (data/random-battles/gen3/sets.json). The
# reachable half of the same bug is `twoturnmove`: Solar Beam is on 4 species
# (victreebel, exeggutor, tangela, sunflora), and the engine charged TWO PP per
# use instead of one. Hyper Beam (slaking) is the mustrecharge case, already
# correct because the engine models the recharge turn as No Move. One guard fixes
# all of them.
#
# The charge-move execute turn needs a local: the engine clears the charge
# volatile before the deduction runs, so `locked_continuation` is captured at the
# clear site. The LOCKEDMOVE volatile covers Outrage-class continuations, where
# it is still present at deduction time. Both are absent on the turn that STARTS
# the lock -- the charge volatile is applied by the move's own effects, after the
# deduction -- so the first turn still pays exactly once, and the next use pays
# again.
#
# Also settles the PP-exhaustion question empirically rather than by reasoning: a
# two-turn move STARTED on the last PP still completes its lock, because the
# execute turn never consults PP again. Verified against the real sim -- 8 PP of
# Sky Attack yields eight complete uses, the eighth beginning at 1 PP. Pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_lockedmove_pp.rs; touches
# generate_instructions_from_move in gen3/generate_instructions.rs only; authored
# against the pp-ordering-patched tree, whose relocated deduction site this
# guard wraps -- the two are one story and the guard has no meaning without it.
poke-engine-gen3-lockedmove-pp.patch


# gen3 Solar Beam is weakened by RAIN, SAND and HAIL only -- never in clear
# weather. Showdown's `solarbeam.onBasePower` (data/moves.ts, inherited unchanged
# by gen3) halves the base power for
# raindance/primordialsea/sandstorm/hail/snowscape, of which gen3 has three; sun
# is a different mechanism entirely (`onTryMove` skips the charge turn without
# touching power).
#
# The engine asked `weather_is_active(&state.weather.weather_type)`. That helper
# is `self.weather.weather_type == argument && not suppressed by Air Lock /
# Cloud Nine`, so feeding it the CURRENT weather reduces to "weather is not
# suppressed" -- true in clear weather too, because NONE == NONE. Every Solar
# Beam therefore did HALF damage, in every branch.
#
# The idiom itself is fine and is left alone at the three other sites that use it
# (MORNINGSUN/MOONLIGHT/SYNTHESIS, the Chlorophyll/Swift Swim speed boost, and
# update_forecast); each pairs it with a `match` on the specific weather, so
# Weather::NONE falls through harmlessly. Only Solar Beam used it as "some
# weather is up".
#
# Found via the two-turn release-damage audit (ledger J.4), which measured
# Showdown -74 against engine -41 non-crit / -163 crit and read the ~4x spread
# between the engine's own branches as a second bug -- the non-crit halving base
# power while the crit did not. It is not: `calculate_damage` derives both
# branches from the SAME choice, so a base-power error cannot separate them. The
# 4x is Light Screen, which gen3 crits correctly ignore, and it is now pinned in
# both directions (2x with no screen, 4x with one) so the diagnosis cannot be
# re-litigated. One root cause, not two: -41 doubles to ~82, and Showdown's -74
# is that at a 0.90 roll.
#
# Verified vs real gen3 Showdown (Exeggutor into Blissey): clear -136, sand -71,
# sun -131 with no charge turn at all. Pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_solarbeam_weather.rs and the
# solarbeamclear/solarbeamsand/solarbeamsun differential scenarios. Touches
# modify_choice in gen3/choice_effects.rs only; authored against the
# lockedmove-pp-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-solarbeam-weather.patch

# gen3 fixed-damage moves must route through a Substitute.
#
# Audit of every damaging arm of choice_special_effect against the guard set the
# normal damage path applies. None of these moves carries `bypasssub` in the gen3
# data, so all five must be absorbed by a Substitute; all five wrote damage
# STRAIGHT to the Pokemon instead:
#   SEISMICTOSS            17/393 sets, on-distribution — the confirmed bug
#   COUNTER, MIRRORCOAT     1/393 each (Wobbuffet, which carries BOTH on its one
#                           set — so the counter-move half of this fix is live in
#                           the pool, not latent)
#   SUPERFANG, ENDEAVOR     0/393 each — fixed anyway, same handler
#
# Showdown's rule is substitute.onTryPrimaryHit (data/moves.ts; gen3 adds no
# override): the move's own damage is computed against the POKEMON — Super Fang
# still halves the mon's HP, Endeavor still reads the mon's HP — then capped at
# the substitute's remaining HP, with NO overflow onto the Pokemon when it
# exceeds. Verified against the real sim: Seismic Toss (100) into a 65 HP
# Substitute answers `-end <target> Substitute` and emits no `-damage` on the
# Pokemon at all; into a 115 HP Substitute it answers
# `-activate <target> Substitute [damage]` and the mon is untouched.
#
# The other guards were audited and found ALREADY CORRECT, and are pinned rather
# than changed:
#   Protect  — one `if blocked_by_protect { return; }` at the top of the
#              dispatcher covers every arm (poke-engine-gen3-rapidspin-fidelity).
#   immunity — Seismic Toss is Fighting-typed but the zero-effectiveness set of
#              Normal and of Fighting is the same single gen3 type (Ghost), so
#              the shared NORMAL probe returns the identical verdict; Super Fang
#              and Endeavor are Normal-typed and correct as written; Counter's
#              Ghost test and Mirror Coat's Dark test match their real types.
#   PAINSPLIT — already skips entirely when a Substitute is up, which is what
#              Showdown does (no bypasssub, and getDamage returns nothing, so the
#              move fails). 4/393 sets (Dusclops, Misdreavus, Swalot, Weezing),
#              so this is the second most reachable arm here and its
#              already-correct verdict is load-bearing, not incidental.
#
# Left unimplemented, documented per the reachability convention: NIGHTSHADE and
# DRAGONRAGE emit no instructions at all (the Flail gap shape), both 0 of 393
# sets. PSYWAVE likewise 0 of 393.
#
# Verified vs real gen3 Showdown (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py:
# seismictosssub / seismictosssubbreak / seismictossghost / seismictosscontrol);
# pinned by rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_fixed_damage_fidelity.rs. Touches
# gen3/choice_effects.rs only; authored against the head of the list, applied
# before the fixture refresh.
poke-engine-gen3-fixed-damage-substitute.patch
# gen3 Toxic: a Poison-type user does NOT bypass the accuracy roll.
#
# Showdown gates that never-miss rule on GENERATION 8, in two places
# (sim/battle-actions.ts:622 and :726):
#     this.battle.gen >= 8 && move.id === 'toxic' && pokemon.hasType('Poison')
# and the base move data points at it rather than implementing it as a move
# effect ("No Guard-like effect for Poison-type users implemented in
# Scripts#tryMoveHit"). Upstream applied it to every generation, so a Poison-type
# Toxic came out of the engine as ONE branch at 100% carrying the poison.
#
# The accuracy value itself was already right: 85, from gen4's override of the
# base 90 (gen3 inherits gen4, the same rule as Wish and Sleep Talk). So the
# whole fix is deleting the bypass arm from gen3's modify_choice.
#
# Reachability is narrower than the headline "Toxic is 152/393 sets": ONLY a
# Poison-type user trips this. That is 8 of 393 sets — ariados, crobat, dustox,
# muk, roselia, swalot, tentacruel, weezing — still well above the bar, and on
# the pool's most common move, but the other 144 Toxic sets were already priced
# correctly at 85/15.
#
# This was NOT a class failure of status-move accuracy. Every imperfect-accuracy
# status move in the pool was probed against the engine and already branches at
# its real gen3 accuracy, walked through the FULL inheritance chain (gen3 ->
# gen4 -> ... -> current) rather than a truncated one:
#
#     move          gen3 acc   sets     engine branches
#     hypnosis        60        14        60 / 40   ok
#     lovelykiss      75         1        75 / 25   ok
#     stunspore       75         7        75 / 25   ok
#     willowisp       75         8        75 / 25   ok
#     sleeppowder     75        14        75 / 25   ok
#     toxic           85       152        85 / 15   ok for a NON-Poison user
#     leechseed       90        12        90 / 10   ok
#     thunderwave    100        33        single    ok - perfect in gen3
#
# Thunder Wave is worth spelling out: it is 100 in gen3 and 90 in current data,
# so a truncated chain that skips gen6/gen7 reports 90 and makes the engine's
# single branch look like a missing miss branch. It is not.
#
# Verified vs real gen3 Showdown (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py:
# toxicmiss / toxichit, on chosen seeds so both sides of the roll are
# deterministic rather than banded); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_status_accuracy_fidelity.rs. Touches
# gen3/choice_effects.rs only; applied before the fixture refresh.
poke-engine-gen3-toxic-accuracy.patch


# Refreshes UPSTREAM fixtures in tests/test_gen3.rs that encode pre-patch
# behaviour. Touches tests only — no engine code — and must stay LAST in this
# list, because its expectations are the behaviour every patch above it leaves
# behind. Adding a behaviour patch after this one without re-checking the
# upstream suite would silently invalidate these fixtures again.
#
# Currently covers the five fixtures invalidated by residual-defer-on-faint,
# which flags a fainted side as owing a replacement via ToggleSideXForceSwitch.
# The five predate that instruction and asserted the exact instruction stream, so
# they failed on the vendored tree while the engine was correct. In every one the
# end-of-turn residual block is EMPTY, so the deferral has no other observable
# effect and the sole delta is the flag: test_rest_does_not_activate_when_fainted,
# test_branch_when_a_roll_can_kill, test_gen3_branch_when_a_roll_can_kill,
# test_fast_explosion_makes_other_side_unable_to_move, test_same_speed_branch.

# gen3: the end-of-turn residual block STOPS when a faint ends the battle. Showdown's
# `Battle.fieldEvent` loop does `this.faintMessages(); if (this.ended) return;` after
# every entry, so the faint-causing entry completes and every remaining handler is
# skipped — the WINNER's own late-ordered residuals included, and even the `upkeep`
# line. The engine ran the block to completion, which manufactured phantom heals and
# ticks after `|win|` and cascaded into every HP-driven residual downstream (32 of
# 298 residue rows, census-decidable by the `|win|` line). Mutually exclusive with
# the residual deferral above by construction: a deferral needs a replacement to be
# owed, which needs a living Pokemon to send. Pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_battle_end_residuals.rs. Touches
# gen3/generate_instructions.rs only.
poke-engine-gen3-battle-end-residuals.patch

# gen3 end-of-turn residual ordering: SPEED-MAJOR, not section-major.
# `Battle.fieldEvent('Residual')` speed-sorts ONE handler list
# (sim/battle.ts:507) with `comparePriority` (sim/battle.ts:404-411): order ASC,
# priority DESC, SPEED DESC, subOrder ASC, effectOrder ASC. Within an order class
# the faster Pokemon therefore resolves its WHOLE residual set before the slower
# one resolves any -- and in gen3 almost everything (abilities 10.3, items 10.4,
# Leech Seed 10.5, status 10.6, partial trap 10.9, Encore/Taunt/Yawn 10.14/15/19)
# is one class, because gen3 keeps the pre-gen5 numbering (`Dex.mod('gen3')`, via
# data/mods/gen3/items.ts and data/mods/gen4/{items,abilities}.ts). Everything
# before this patch batched section-major across both sides.
#
# Also folds in what that reordering exposed: the ability class (10.3) runs
# BEFORE the item class (10.4) rather than after status damage, the threshold
# berries share Leftovers' 10.4 slot, Wish is order 7 (ahead of the weather chip
# at 8), Reflect/Light Screen are side orders 1/2, and Future Sight is order 11
# (after both sides' status damage, not before). The old "order 5" split is
# removed: 5.x is the gen5+ table, which gen3 does not use.
#
# Speed ties are RANDOM -- `speedSort` finishes a tie with `prng.shuffle`
# (sim/battle.ts:455-457) -- so a tie is a 50/50 fork in
# `add_end_of_turn_branches`, collapsed back to one branch when both orders
# produce the identical instruction list. Exports `get_effective_speed` and
# `residual_speed_order` so the search crate's residual renderer can build its
# positional attribution plan against the same order. Ground truth for every
# ordering claim: scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py scenarios
# `residualspeedmajor*` / `residualspeedpara*` / `residualspeedtie` and the
# native pins in rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_residual_speed_order.rs.
# Touches gen3/{abilities,items,generate_instructions}.rs.
poke-engine-gen3-residual-speed-order.patch
# gen3 Rest FAILS at full HP.
#
# `rest.onTry` (data/moves.ts — NO gen mod anywhere in the chain overrides Rest,
# so gen3 inherits the base directly) fails in this order:
#
#     1. status === 'slp' || hasAbility('comatose')  -> return false
#     2. hp === maxhp   -> `-fail <user> heal`, return null
#     3. hasAbility('insomnia')     -> `-fail ... ability: Insomnia`
#     4. hasAbility('vitalspirit')  -> `-fail ... ability: Vital Spirit`
#
# Upstream guarded only (1), so a full-HP Rest slept the user. The divergence is
# STATUS-level rather than heal-level: the spurious sleep SUPPRESSED an incoming
# status that Showdown lets land, changing the legal action set for the rest of
# the battle. Verified against the real sim on the repro shape — a full-HP Xatu
# Resting into a Toxic answers `-fail|p1a: Xatu|heal` and then `-status|p1a:
# Xatu|tox`, where upstream slept it and the Toxic never landed.
#
# (3) and (4) are deliberately NOT modelled: Comatose is a gen7 ability, and no
# gen3 randbats set pairs Rest with Insomnia or Vital Spirit (0 of the 55 Rest
# sets), so neither is reachable. If they ever become reachable, note that the
# full-HP check comes FIRST, so a full-HP Insomnia user fails with the heal
# message rather than the ability one.
#
# The failure costs the turn AND the PP, in both engines: Showdown deducts PP in
# `runMove` (battle-actions.ts:282) before `useMove` fires the `Try` event
# (:585), and the engine decrements PP in generate_instructions.rs:2370, well
# before this dispatcher at :2417. So skipping the effect reproduces `-fail`
# exactly, with no PP plumbing needed.
#
# Reachability: Rest is on 55 of 393 sets, and the full-HP case is the one the
# ledger's residue rows are made of (14/14).
#
# Verified vs real gen3 Showdown (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py:
# restfullhp / restdamagedcontrol); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_rest_fidelity.rs. Touches
# gen3/choice_effects.rs only; applied before the fixture refresh.
poke-engine-gen3-rest-fullhp.patch
# gen3 Pain Split clamps to each mon's OWN maxhp.
#
# `painsplit.onHit` (data/moves.ts — no gen mod in the chain overrides Pain
# Split, so gen3 inherits the base) averages the two HP values and assigns each
# side through `Pokemon#sethp`:
#
#     const averagehp = Math.floor((targetHP + pokemon.hp) / 2) || 1;
#     target.sethp(target.hp - (targetHP - averagehp));
#     pokemon.sethp(averagehp);
#
# and `sethp` (sim/pokemon.ts:1656) is where the clamping lives:
#
#     if (!this.hp) return 0;          // fainted: no-op
#     d = trunc(d); if (d < 1) d = 1;  // floor at 1, NOT 0
#     if (this.hp > this.maxhp) this.hp = this.maxhp;   // clamp, per mon
#
# So the average floors ONCE, is floored at 1, and is then clamped against each
# Pokemon's own maximum. Upstream assigned the raw average to BOTH actives, so
# the mon with the smaller maxhp came out ABOVE its maximum: hp > maxhp, a
# corrupt state that every later damage/heal/faint check then reads. That is 12
# of the 15 remaining Pain Split residue rows.
#
# Verified against the real sim: a full 271-max Weezing splitting with a full
# 341-max Groudon averages 306 — Groudon lands on 306/341 UNCLAMPED (306 < 341)
# and Weezing on 271/271 CLAMPED, where upstream gave Weezing 306/271.
#
# SCOPE NOTE, so the #915 audit table is not read as contradicted: that audit
# verdicted this arm "correct as-is", and that verdict STANDS. It was about
# Substitute routing — Pain Split correctly skips behind a sub, matching
# Showdown's `getDamage`-returns-nothing failure — and it covered the guard set,
# not the assignment arithmetic underneath it, which is where this bug lives.
# The sub-skip behaviour is re-pinned alongside the clamp so the two cannot drift
# apart.
#
# Reachability: Pain Split is on 4 of 393 sets (Dusclops, Misdreavus, Swalot,
# Weezing) — the second most reachable arm in choice_special_effect after Seismic
# Toss.
#
# Verified vs real gen3 Showdown (scripts/gen3_switch_differential.py:
# painsplitclamp / painsplitcontrol); pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_painsplit_fidelity.rs. Touches
# gen3/choice_effects.rs only; applied before the fixture refresh.
poke-engine-gen3-painsplit-clamp.patch
# gen3 consecutive-Protect success FLOORS at 1/8.
#
# gen3 resolves `stall` through gen4's `{ inherit: true, counterMax: 8 }`, and
# that `inherit: true` resolves to GEN5's full definition, NOT to base — the
# fifth inheritance direction recorded in the ledger's Dex-resolution rule. The
# counter starts at 2 and doubles under a test-before-multiply gate,
# `if (counter < counterMax) counter *= 2`, so it walks 2 -> 4 -> 8 and then
# STOPS because `8 < 8` is false. The chance is 1/counter:
#
#     attempt   1     2     3     4     5     6 ...
#     gen3      1    1/2   1/4   1/8   1/8   1/8
#     upstream  1    1/2   1/4   1/8  1/16  1/32
#
# The ladder first REACHES 1/8 at the 4th attempt, which upstream already priced
# correctly. Upstream first DIVERGES at the 5th, where it keeps halving past the
# cap. Clamping the exponent at 3 reproduces the cap exactly (0.5^3 == 1/8).
#
# EVIDENCE BASIS, stated plainly because it differs from most patches here: the
# floor itself is NOT empirically confirmed against the sim and is not claimed to
# be. The 5th consecutive Protect needs four consecutive successes —
# 1 * 1/2 * 1/4 * 1/8 = 1/64, about 1.6% of sequences — so no affordable sample
# separates 1/8 from 1/16 there. What IS measured (160 seeds) is the x2 ladder
# the floor sits on: 2nd attempt 239/496 = 0.482, 3rd 40/204 = 0.196, which is
# ~7 sigma from the x3 reading that a base-data walk produces. That measurement
# is what makes the resolved reading trustworthy; the cap is then read off the
# same resolved definition and pinned at the engine level both ways.
#
# Pinned by rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_protect_floor_fidelity.rs, which
# keeps attempts 1-4 as controls: they pass with and without this patch, so a
# change that moved them would be altering behaviour the measurement endorses.
# Touches the consecutive-Protect branch in gen3/generate_instructions.rs only;
# applied before the fixture refresh.
poke-engine-gen3-protect-floor.patch

# gen3 Guts/Facade wake-turn phantom boost. before_move's choice modification
# (ability_modify_attack_being_used / modify_choice) runs BEFORE the sleep and
# freeze branching in generate_instructions_from_move, but a sleeping or frozen
# attacker's move only executes on the branch that cured the status first —
# Showdown cures in slp.onBeforeMove (data/mods/gen3/conditions.ts) and reads
# Guts at damage time via onModifyAtk (data/abilities.ts), and the engine's own
# wake branch sets status NONE before damage lands. Upstream keyed both boosts
# off the PRE-turn status, so a Guts user's wake-turn attack carried a phantom
# 1.5x (Facade: 2x). Sleep Talk-called moves execute while still asleep and
# keep the boost. Repro rows: seeds 1500025/7,98 1500164/67 1500030/82
# (Hariyama/Machamp, observed = unboosted rolls, engine = 1.5x high).
# Touches the GUTS arm in gen3/abilities.rs and the FACADE arm in
# gen3/choice_effects.rs.
poke-engine-gen3-guts-facade-wake-turn.patch

# gen3 Trace copies WITHOUT activating the copied ability. sim/pokemon.ts
# setAbility() fires the copied ability's 'Start' event only when
# `battle.gen > 3`, and gen3's trace override (data/mods/gen3/abilities.ts)
# calls plain setAbility — so a gen3 traced Intimidate never drops the foe's
# Attack and a traced weather ability never sets weather. Upstream ran the
# switch-in activation match on the copied ability. Passive effects (the
# status/volatile cures, Forecast recompute) still apply. Repro row: seed
# 1500222/17 (Porygon2 traces Intimidate; Showdown shows no -unboost, engine
# dropped Mightyena's Attack and undershot its Hidden Power by 1.5x).
# Touches ability_on_switch_in in gen3/abilities.rs; authored against the
# guts-facade-wake-turn tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-trace-no-activation.patch

# gen3 stepwise damage truncation. RSE applies damage modifiers in a fixed
# order with an integer floor at EVERY step (data/mods/gen3/scripts.ts
# modifyDamage: burn -> screens -> spread -> weather -> physical min-1 -> +2 ->
# crit -> STAB -> per-type-step effectiveness, 85-100 roll LAST). Upstream
# multiplied all modifiers in f32 and floored once at the end, carrying
# fractions through the x2 steps that the sim drops: STAB on an odd (base+2)
# into a super-effective x2 leaves the engine's max roll 1 point above the
# sim's, so real bottom rolls (85-86%) fall just outside the engine's legal
# roll set. That is the cycle-seven brief's 0.90-0.917 observed/engine cluster
# (engine branch damage is the 0.925 average of an inflated max). Repro rows:
# 1500229/3 (Jirachi Psychic: engine max 159 vs sim 158, observed 134 = sim's
# min roll), 1500201/16 (Light Ball Pikachu Thunderbolt: 243 vs 242, observed
# 205 = sim's min roll). Rewrites common_pkmn_damage_calc as the sim's integer
# pipeline (burn/weather floored pre-+2, crit x2 inside, STAB floored, two
# type steps floored) and moves the crit multiplier inside; screens and the
# rare volatile modifiers keep their trailing float position (screens are
# pool-unreachable). Touches gen3/damage_calc.rs only; authored against the
# trace-no-activation tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-damage-stepwise-truncation.patch

# gen3 self-destruct faints the user only if the move actually EXECUTES. Showdown
# reaches it in `useMoveInner` (sim/battle-actions.ts:501):
#
#     if (this.battle.gen !== 4 && move.selfdestruct === 'always') {
#         this.battle.faint(pokemon, pokemon, move);
#     }
#
# and `runMove` calls `useMove` only after the `BeforeMove` gate returns true, so a
# fully-paralyzed / asleep / frozen Pokemon never explodes. The engine applied the
# faint in `choice_before_move`, which runs BEFORE
# generate_instructions_from_existing_status_conditions rolls those immobilizers, so
# the BLOCKED branch killed its own user. The visible symptom was a missing Leftovers
# tick on that branch -- residuals correctly do not run for a dead mon -- which is why
# the family was first read as "blocked branches drop the residual block". They do
# not: an ordinary blocked move keeps its residuals (pinned as a control).
#
# The relocation keeps the faint BEFORE damage (gen3 fains the user first) and keeps
# it firing through Protect, both matching Showdown, where it precedes `tryMoveHit`.
# The DAMP guard is preserved. Sleep Talk's callee still reaches it, correctly: the
# called move runs through `useMove` like any other.
#
# Touches gen3/choice_effects.rs (removal) and gen3/generate_instructions.rs
# (relocation); authored against the lastmove-semantics tree, applied before the
# fixture refresh. Pinned by rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_selfdestruct_gate.rs.
poke-engine-gen3-explosion-selfdestruct-gate.patch
# gen3 stat-modifier flooring (mechanism 2 of the damage_calc lane). RSE
# applies the item/ability stat modifiers to the boost-floored STAT via
# battle.modify's 4096-based fixed point BEFORE the base formula's /Defense
# and /50 truncations (sim/battle-actions.ts getDamage: calculateStat ->
# ModifyAtk/ModifySpA/ModifyDef/ModifySpD events -> the truncated base
# formula; every effective-gen3 handler chainModifies, Hustle modifies the
# stat directly). Upstream multiplied choice.base_power in f32, carrying the
# modifier's half-point through the /D and /50 floors: Choice Band on an odd
# attack stat left the engine max 1-2 points above the sim's, so real bottom
# rolls fell outside the engine's legal roll set. Repro rows: 1500221/13
# (Choice Band Pidgeot Aerial Ace: engine max 123 vs sim 121; observed 102 =
# sim's exact min roll, engine legal floor 104) and 1500024/9 (Guts+psn -1
# atk Ursaring Return: engine 120 vs sim 118). Also folds in, per the same
# sim reading: Light Ball is SpA-only in gen3 (mods/gen3/items.ts kills the
# inherited Atk half; upstream doubled physical too), Thick Club is Atk-only,
# Metal Powder is x2 Def for an UNTRANSFORMED Ditto physical-only (upstream:
# /1.5 any category), Dragon Scale has no boost (bare evolution item),
# Explosion/Self-Destruct halve the MODIFIED defense stat with a floor
# (clampIntRange(floor(def/2),1)) instead of doubling BP, gen3 Plus/Minus
# fire across the field (getAllActive - a Minun facing a Plusle is boosted),
# and the upstream Guts burn-compensation double is dropped: with patch 33's
# Guts-guarded burn halving it triple-counted a burned Guts attacker (3x
# instead of the sim's 1.5x). Touches gen3/damage_calc.rs (new fixed-point
# stat-modifier chains), gen3/items.rs, gen3/abilities.rs and
# gen3/choice_effects.rs (the relocated arms removed); authored against the
# explosion-selfdestruct-gate tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-stat-modifier-flooring.patch

# gen3 type-effectiveness netting. The sim NETS the type exponent first
# (typeMod = runEffectiveness sums +1/-1 across the defender's types) and
# only then applies |typeMod| steps of the net sign (data/mods/gen3/
# scripts.ts modifyDamage:88-104). Patch 33's transcription applied the two
# types as independent steps, flooring inside a net-neutral (2x, 0.5x) pair
# whenever the resisted type comes first in the defender's type tuple:
# floor(v/2)*2 = v-1 for odd v where the sim leaves v untouched. Repro row:
# 1500076/96 (HP Grass into Shuckle, BUG/ROCK: sim max 29, engine max 28;
# observed 29 = the sim's exact 100% roll, above the engine's legal max).
# Touches the type step in gen3/damage_calc.rs common_pkmn_damage_calc only;
# authored against the stat-modifier-flooring tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-type-effectiveness-netting.patch

# gen3 weather-move targeting. Rain Dance / Sunny Day / Hail / Sandstorm are
# field moves: they never TryHit the opposing Pokemon, so the defender-side
# ability interceptors must not see them. The engine's Choice::default gave
# them target: Opponent, sailing them past ability_modify_attack_against's own
# targeting guard (whose comment names Rain Dance as the case it exists to
# stop) and into the absorb arms: Water Absorb healed maxhp/4 off an opposing
# Rain Dance (repro row 1500124/58), and Flash Fire would eat an opposing
# Sunny Day the same way. Sets target: MoveTarget::User on the four weather
# moves in the shared MOVES table; authored against the
# type-effectiveness-netting tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-weather-move-targeting.patch

# gen3 recoil rounding. The sim computes recoil as
# clampIntRange(floor(damageDealt * recoil[0] / recoil[1]), 1) with Double-Edge
# at [1,3] (gen4 mod, inherited); the engine multiplied by f32 0.33/0.25/0.5
# and truncated, so a max-roll Double-Edge recoil was floor(0.33*75) = 24
# where the sim deals floor(75/3) = 25 (repro row 1500207/27), and a recoil
# that truncated to 0 was dropped instead of clamped to 1. Maps the stored
# fraction back to the exact rational at the single application site in
# gen3/generate_instructions.rs; authored against the weather-move-targeting
# tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-recoil-rounding.patch

# gen3 fixed-damage pipeline. The fixed/level/fraction-damage arms applied
# their damage directly inside choice_special_effect, and because
# calculate_damage returns (0,0) for a zero-BP move, check_move_hit_or_miss
# zeroed percent_hit and run_move's entire post-damage suite never ran for
# them: no set_damage_dealt (Counter after Seismic Toss returned nothing, row
# 1500192/91), no defender contact abilities (Rough Skin rows 1500103/76 and
# 1500274/15, Flame Body row 1500287/76), no Destiny Bond, no Endure, and
# Super Fang's 90% accuracy was never rolled. Showdown treats these as
# ordinary damaging moves with a damageCallback (sim/battle-actions.ts
# getDamage:1611). New gen3_fixed_damage_amount computes the callback value
# (Seismic Toss/Night Shade level with the gen3 immunity probes, Super Fang
# clampIntRange(floor(hp/2),1) - fixing upstream's ceiling and its deals-
# nothing-at-1hp arm - Endeavor's difference, Counter/Mirror Coat 2x
# damage_dealt) and the move flows through the normal damage path with no
# roll spread and no crit branch. Night Shade dealt no damage at all before
# this patch (ledger Appendix K.3). Touches gen3/generate_instructions.rs and
# gen3/choice_effects.rs (direct-apply arms removed); authored against the
# recoil-rounding tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-fixed-damage-pipeline.patch

# gen3 Counter/Mirror Coat Hidden Power semantics. gen3 Showdown counts a
# Hidden Power hit as PHYSICAL for Counter and NEVER for Mirror Coat,
# whatever its IV-derived elemental type - the clauses are explicit in
# data/mods/gen3/moves.ts (counter onDamage: category === 'Physical' ||
# effect.id === 'hiddenpower'; mirrorcoat: category === 'Special' &&
# effect.id !== 'hiddenpower'). The engine recorded damage_dealt with the
# choice's type-derived category, so a special-typed Hidden Power was Mirror
# Coat-bounceable (repro rows 1500155/22 and 1500264/40: the sim's Mirror
# Coat did nothing, the engine retaliated 2x) and invisible to Counter.
# damage_dealt now records Hidden Power as Physical; authored against the
# fixed-damage-pipeline tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-counter-hiddenpower-category.patch

# gen3 Flash Fire position. The boosted volatile is a ModifyDamagePhase1
# handler in gen3 (data/mods/gen4/abilities.ts flashfire condition, inherited)
# - it chains with screens and floors at 4096 scale BEFORE the +2/crit/STAB/
# type steps. The engine applied it as a trailing float multiplier AFTER the
# type steps, one point high on resisted boosted Fire moves: repro row
# 1500123/79 (Flash-Fired Ninetales Fire Blast into Octillery: sim max 92,
# engine 93, observed 78 = the sim's exact minimum roll). Moves the 1.5x into
# the stepwise pipeline between burn and weather using the fixed-point
# helpers; screens keep their trailing caller position (pool-unreachable per
# the damage_calc brief). Touches gen3/damage_calc.rs only; authored against
# the counter-hiddenpower-category tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-flashfire-phase1.patch

# gen3 recharge-turn residuals. A Hyper Beam recharge turn is a FULL turn:
# the recharging side's only option is None, but Showdown runs the whole
# end-of-turn residual block on the |cant|<mon>|recharge boundary (sim probe:
# Leftovers heal + toxic tick both fire on a (switch, recharge) turn).
# end_of_turn_triggered's bare (Switch, None) exclusion - correct for
# faint-replacement plies, whose residuals already ran or were deferred on
# the ply that caused the faint - also swallowed VOLUNTARY switches beside a
# recharging Pokemon, dropping every residual (the certification sweep's
# 56-row family, all exactly this shape at 100% branch; e.g. 2000204/51:
# Leech Seed, Leftovers and psn all observed-only). Distinguisher: on a
# recharge turn the None side still carries MUSTRECHARGE when the trigger is
# evaluated. Touches end_of_turn_triggered in gen3/generate_instructions.rs
# only; authored against the flashfire-phase1 tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-recharge-turn-residuals.patch

# gen3 absorb abilities vs Protect and accuracy. The sim reaches an absorb
# ability's onTryHit only AFTER Protect has blocked the move and the accuracy
# roll has passed (sim probes: protecting Vaporeon answers -activate with no
# absorb; missed Hydro Pump answers -miss with no absorb). The engine's
# Water/Volt Absorb (and Dry Skin) arms call remove_all_effects(), which
# clears flags.protect and forces accuracy to 100 (VOLTABSORB re-forced 100
# explicitly), so the converted quarter-heal pierced Protect (before_move's
# Protect gate never saw the flag) and healed on the sim's miss rolls - the
# sweep's 39-row absorb family (23 protect-shape + 16 miss-shape; e.g.
# 2000214/12 protected, 2000628/72 missed Hydro Pump). Preserves the original
# accuracy and protect flag through the conversion; the existing Protect
# stripping then clears the heal, and the accuracy split leaves the heal off
# the miss branch. Touches the three arms in gen3/abilities.rs only; authored
# against the recharge-turn-residuals tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-absorb-protect-accuracy.patch

# gen3 typed Hidden Power thaw exclusion. The thaw-on-fire-hit exclusion in
# generate_instructions.rs listed only the generic Choices::HIDDENPOWER (and
# WEATHERBALL), so pokezero's typed variants (HIDDENPOWERFIRE70 etc.) thawed a
# frozen defender unconditionally and let it act — the certification sweep's
# 4-row freeze family (e.g. 2000131/47: sim's Omastar stays frozen and cants;
# engine emits ChangeStatus FREEZE -> NONE at 100% and Omastar attacks). The
# sim never thaws on Hidden Power: its runtime move id is always the generic
# hiddenpower (dex type Normal in gen3's frz.onDamagingHit; the typed name is
# display-only in the request payload) — verified on the vendored checkout and
# by live gen3customgame probes (HP-Fire IVs supereffective on Skarmory, no
# thaw on a frozen Shuckle; Flamethrower control thaws). The exclusion now
# enumerates all 33 Hidden Power variants, the same set as the
# counter-hiddenpower-category patch above. The 80/20 self-thaw gate and real
# Fire-move thaws are untouched. Touches the one condition in
# gen3/generate_instructions.rs; authored against the absorb tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-typed-hiddenpower-thaw.patch

# Public no-op branch identity. Accuracy is rolled before Protect in Showdown,
# but remove_effects_for_protect forced it to 100 and then duplicate-state
# folding erased the miss-vs-Protect distinction. Full-HP absorb hits had the
# same empty-delta collision with misses. Preserve accuracy and attach a
# reversible zero-heal marker only to successful Protect/absorb hit branches;
# the Rust protocol mapper consumes that marker into the correct public event.
# Authored against the typed-hiddenpower-thaw tree above.
poke-engine-gen3-public-noop-branches.patch

poke-engine-gen3-upstream-fixture-refresh.patch

poke-engine-gen3-forecast-suppressor-handoff.patch
