poke-engine-gen3-review-compositions.patch

# Gen 3 successful Substitute ends an existing partial-trap volatile. Showdown
# silently ends Wrap / Bind / Fire Spin / Clamp / Whirlpool after the Substitute
# is created, before end-of-turn residuals. Upstream leaves PARTIALLYTRAPPED in
# place, emitting an extra 1/16 chip on that same boundary (retained identity
# 3101100/29). The removal is strictly inside Substitute's successful-cost arm:
# failed Substitute attempts, ordinary trapped turns, Rapid Spin, and the
# source-leaves / Baton Pass lifecycle rules are unchanged. Pinned by
# rust/pokezero-search/tests/gen3_switch_fidelity.rs; authored against the
# review-compositions tree above. No upstream fixture patch changes, so the
# frozen fixture-refresh entry remains unmodified.
poke-engine-gen3-wrap-substitute-lifecycle.patch
poke-engine-gen3-toxic-stage-cap.patch

# gen3 forced-replacement recharge timing. A Hyper Beam KO makes the defender
# replace before the waiting attacker reaches Showdown's onBeforeMove hook.
# The engine removed MUSTRECHARGE during that compulsory replacement, then
# skipped the attacker's actual recharge turn. Defer removal while the opponent
# still has force_switch; the existing pending-force-switch mapper path already
# owns that replacement boundary. Pinned by the real KO/replacement sequence in
# tests/test_engine_recharge_absorb_fidelity.py. This entry must remain after
# the frozen stack above because older zero-context fallback patches retain
# their exact application positions.
poke-engine-gen3-recharge-forced-replacement.patch

# C27 crit-arm kill split. The gen3 brancher already partitions the KO
# threshold when the NON-CRIT roll range straddles it, using
# compare_health_with_damage_multiples for exact masses and an exact non-kill
# representative. The sibling path -- non-crit can never kill -- split crit from
# non-crit but collapsed the crit arm to its AVERAGE roll, so when the crit
# range straddled the defender's HP the other side of that threshold was absent
# from the branch support entirely. The engine then asserted a KO a legal crit
# roll would not have scored (or the reverse), which the tree prices as full
# crit mass on one outcome at exactly the tactical margins. Applies the existing
# identity to the crit arm rather than standing a second partitioner beside it,
# and fixes that identity dropping a roll landing EXACTLY on the defender's HP
# from both buckets -- exact-equal is lethal, and its mass was silently priced
# as a survival. Measured before the patch in
# reports/c27_kill_split_premeasure.json.
poke-engine-gen3-crit-kill-split.patch

# C31 Substitute quarter-HP gate. gen3 already preserved all sixteen damage rolls
# when the defender had a pending Flail or Reversal, because an average roll
# "erases those reachable positions before the second move reads HP". Substitute
# reads the same HP for the same reason -- gen3 refuses it unless the user is
# above a quarter of its maximum -- and the predicate simply did not list it. So a
# crit range straddling that quarter had the representative roll decide whether
# the Substitute happened at all, dropping the other side from the branch support
# (seed 17000037 step 55: eight of sixteen Psychic crit rolls leave Gyarados'
# Substitute failing; the representative roll succeeds, Showdown's roll did not).
# Extends the existing predicate rather than adding a second partitioner beside
# C27's kill split. Registered in reports/c31_substitute_threshold_prediction.json.
poke-engine-gen3-substitute-hp-gate.patch
# CONFUSION snap-out TIMING. The duration patch above forks the expiry ladder at
# end of turn, but Showdown does not show it there: `confusion.onBeforeMove`
# decrements, snaps out at zero and lets the move through, so `-end confusion`
# lands on the victim's NEXT MOVE ATTEMPT. Publishing the removal at end of turn
# put a state change a decision boundary early, and the renderer had to discard
# the whole belief world as attribution-unsafe rather than leak it
# (`confusion_expiry_timing_unobservable` -- 35% of residual fallback on the
# restricted band). This splits the two: the PROBABILISTIC fork stays at end of
# turn, where both outcomes are terminal and no move-generation restructuring is
# needed, and only the OBSERVABLE instruction moves to the move attempt, where it
# is DETERMINISTIC because the outcome is already decided. Carried as a negative
# duration sentinel; `chance_confusion_ends` returns 0.0 for <= 0 so a pending
# counter cannot re-enter the ladder, and the volatile stays visible in between --
# which is what Showdown shows. Equivalence measured: per-rung snap-out mass,
# per-rung self-hit mass and the turns-confused marginal are identical to the
# unpatched ladder. Touches gen3/generate_instructions.rs only; authored against
# the confusion-duration-patched tree.
poke-engine-gen3-confusion-snapout-timing.patch

# C87: Sleep Talk callees must branch on damage like any other move. Showdown's
# gen3 override (data/mods/gen3/moves.ts:526) filters the callee set and then
# runs it through this.actions.useMove, which performs the ordinary crit roll.
# Passing branch_on_damage=false sent the callee to the no-crit-arm path, so a
# Sleep-Talk-called crit was reachable in the sim and absent from the support.
# Also clears the stale first_move and balances the 16-roll loop's apply/reverse.
# Registered in reports/c87_sleeptalk_crit_arm_absence.json.
poke-engine-gen3-sleeptalk-crit-arm.patch

# Belly Drum reads the user's own HP as a GATE after the attacker's hit lands:
# gen3 refuses it unless the user is above half its maximum. A damage roll range
# straddling that half decides whether the drum happens at all, so collapsing to
# a representative roll drops one side from the branch support. Exactly the
# Substitute case (maxhp/4) one gate wider (maxhp/2); the per-roll gates
# themselves are faithful, the SUPPORT was incomplete.
# Registered in reports/c96_unattributed_source_level_causes.json.
poke-engine-gen3-bellydrum-roll-gate.patch

# Partition a damage fan on RESIDUAL lethality, not only lethality on the hit.
# reports/c109.
poke-engine-gen3-residual-lethality-partition.patch
poke-engine-gen3-contact-flags.patch

# Let a contact secondary see the attacker WAKE (or thaw) on the same turn.
# `ability_modify_attack_against` runs from `before_move`, one call before
# `generate_instructions_from_existing_status_conditions` resolves the attacker's
# own sleep/freeze, so `contact_status_is_valid` read a status that was about to
# be cured and refused Poison Point, Effect Spore, Flame Body and Static outright.
# Showdown decides these in `onDamagingHit`, after `slp.onBeforeMove` cleared it.
# Ignoring an about-to-be-cured status is exact rather than approximate: every
# branch that keeps the status is one where the move never lands. Sleep Talk and
# the move it calls are the exception and keep refusing. reports/c118.
poke-engine-gen3-a5-wake-before-contact.patch

# Truncate battle-end residuals BETWEEN entries, not mid-entry, for weather.
# battle-end-residuals.patch states the Showdown rule correctly -- the faint-causing
# entry runs to completion, then every remaining handler is skipped -- and then
# installs its guard per SIDE inside the weather loop. Weather is ONE entry chipping
# both actives, so a mon killed by its own sand chip was cancelling the other
# active's chip. Recorded protocol on 19100002/53 emits both chips, then the faint,
# then |win|. The per-Pokemon guards in order 10 are correct and untouched.
# reports/c122.
poke-engine-gen3-weather-entry-truncation.patch

# Row 2 of the era-58 fallback ledger: 781 killed decisions, 28.7% of all fallback,
# and #1093 measured producer A at 0 so this addresses the whole class as observed.
# PLUMBING ONLY -- adds `rest_sleep_pending_refund` to Pokemon and an Instruction
# variant to set it reversibly. NOTHING reads the field yet; no search behaviour
# changes. The consuming emission on switch-in is a separate patch.
#
# The field is a TAGGED trailing value (`refund:<n>`), not a positional one:
# `pre_transform` is appended only when Some, so index 29 exists conditionally and a
# positional append would land on it for every untransformed Pokemon, where
# PreTransform::deserialize indexes split[6 + index] and PANICS. Tagging follows
# LastUsedMove's `move:`/`switch:` idiom. Design and that correction:
# fp-power-deploy reports/evidence/row2-engine-fix-design-20260805.md.
poke-engine-gen3-rest-sleep-pending-refund.patch

# Exposes rest_sleep_pending_refund on the pyo3 Pokemon binding. Needed because
# pokezero builds engine state through the binding (poke_engine_adapter.py:
# engine.State(...)), NOT through State::deserialize -- so the field added by the
# patch above could never reach search without this. The Into<Pokemon> half is the
# dangerous one: it compiles fine while silently writing 0, so it is pinned by
# tests/test_rest_sleep_refund_boundary.py with a nonzero value rather than by the
# compiler.
poke-engine-gen3-rest-sleep-refund-binding.patch

# Implement gen3 White Herb (cause A6). Absent from gen3 entirely -- WHITEHERB
# existed only under src/genx/ -- so a Deoxys never restored the Superpower drop
# and Golem's Rock Slide landed against an undropped Defence in Showdown but a
# dropped one here, flipping the whole roll band. The item is KNOWABLE, not a
# hidden-item limit: teams.ts:471 returns White Herb unconditionally for deoxys
# and deoxysattack. Zeroes NEGATIVE boosts only -- positives are untouched, it is
# not a reset -- and consumes the item. Wired at THREE sites, each checking both
# sides: after a move's boost effect, after get_instructions_from_secondaries,
# and after ability_on_switch_in (Intimidate). Sites 2 and 3 were missing in the
# first version and were added after self-review found the reachability argument
# false. Remaining uncovered producers are Transform/Psych-Up boost copy and
# Trick-style item acquisition, both unreachable: the only holders are deoxys and
# deoxysattack and their movepool carries none of them. reports/c124, c126.
poke-engine-gen3-white-herb.patch


# Consumes rest_sleep_pending_refund: credits it to rest_turns on switch-in
# (before Spikes -- Showdown resolves the sleep counter ahead of entry hazards),
# and voids it whenever the sleep stint ends, so a stale refund cannot be spent
# on an unrelated later switch-in. The clamp to rest_turns <= 3 is a crash guard:
# the wake match panics with "Invalid rest_turns value" above that, confirmed by
# running it. NOT inert: banking on a sleepUsable attempt makes the field nonzero
# during search with no harness involvement, so a Rest + Sleep Talk mon is credited
# on switch-in already. The harness write-side only adds the observed-root case.
poke-engine-gen3-rest-sleep-refund-emission.patch

# the first move's damage roll changes its result directly. Found by the C116

poke-engine-gen3-painsplit-hp-reading.patch

# Scale the KO partition threshold by hit_count. Both partitions compared a
# PER-HIT maximum against the defender's FULL HP, so a multi-hit move whose
# single hit cannot KO never partitioned even when its hits together can.
# Bonemerang on 19100113/62: per-hit max 140 vs 253 HP, so the non-crit arm
# collapsed to one roll -- but two hits reach 280, and rolls 85..90 total
# 238..252 and SURVIVE while 91..100 total 254..280 and kill. Gated on
# hit_count > 1, so single-hit moves are bit-identical. reports/c129.
poke-engine-gen3-hitcount-ko-threshold.patch

# A faint cancels the queued action of every STILL-ACTIVE Pokemon, switches
# included (Showdown faintMessages, sim/battle.ts:2609-2618, over getAllActive()).
# The MoveCategory::Switch arm returned above every cancellation gate, so a switch
# was the one action nothing could cancel. Closes holdout 19100180/24, where both
# sides switch, p2's incoming Pokemon dies to Spikes, and the engine performed p1's
# switch anyway. The predicate is the Showdown rule verbatim -- someone newly
# fainted AND this side is still standing afterwards -- with no Pursuit branch:
# getAllActive() filters on !fainted, so a Pursuit victim (which IS the switcher) is
# outside the set and its switch correctly proceeds. Two earlier attempts each
# implemented one direction only and were withdrawn on their falsifiers; both are
# now pinned by Showdown scenarios and engine tests. Predictions and measurements:
# reports/c136_faint_cancels_prediction.md, with the four sweeps it cites at

poke-engine-gen3-faint-cancels-opposing-switch.patch

# The crit-straddle residual sub-split. When the CRIT fan straddles the KO
# threshold, Case B partitioned it into crit-kill and crit-survive and never
# consulted the residual threshold -- so the residual sub-split existed at two of
# the three partition sites and was missing from the third. Closes dev row
# 19000074/27, where the priced crit fan is
# [214,216,219,221,224,226,229,231,234,236,239,241,244,246,249,252] against 244 HP
# with a sandstorm threshold of 229: Showdown rolled 241, a member of the engine's
# own fan, while the engine emitted arms only at 244 (the HP) and 227 (the mean of
# the twelve non-KO rolls, not a fan member). Mirrors Case A's identity exactly --
# the KO threshold is the band ceiling, so the residual band is
# #{rolls in [229, 244)} and the hit-lethal rolls stay with the KO arm.
# reports/c133_collapsed_roll_disposition.md section 3. Prediction registered at
# reports/c138_collapse_class_engine_fixes_prediction.md; sweeps at
# reports/artifacts/c138_collapsefix_{main,critstraddle}_{dev,holdout}_sweep.json.
poke-engine-gen3-crit-straddle-residual-split.patch

# The status-aware residual threshold (cause A8), and the disjoint-band mass rule
# it forces. `residual_lethality_threshold` read the defender's PRE-MOVE state, so
# a Fire move's own burn secondary was invisible and the split never fired: closes
# holdout rows 19100107/135 (Sacred Fire into Roselia) and 19100191/5 (Fire Blast
# into Ninjask), where the observed roll is a member of the engine's own fan and
# dies to the burn tick. `choice` is now passed in so secondaries are visible, and
# the thresholds form a UNION -- not a minimum, which c133 section 4 measures
# destroying an arm the engine emits today. Because the thresholds are nested, each
# arm carries the DISJOINT band #{rolls in [t_i, t_i+1)} priced at its own t_i,
# with the KO threshold participating as the ceiling wherever a KO arm exists;
# per-arm #{rolls >= t_i} double-counts and overflows 16/16. Applied at all four
# partition sites. reports/c135_roll_divergent_lethality_adjudication.md sections
# 2-3 and 5, reports/c133_collapsed_roll_disposition.md section 4. Predictions and
# measurements: reports/c138_collapse_class_engine_fixes_prediction.md, artifacts
# at reports/artifacts/c138_collapsefix_{main,critstraddle,statusaware}_{dev,holdout}_sweep.json.
poke-engine-gen3-status-aware-residual-threshold.patch

# C116 Phase 2 -- a FLAG-GATED REFERENCE ORACLE, consumed by tests and by nothing
# that ships. Enumerate-then-merge behind the RUNTIME env flag
# POKEZERO_ENUMERATE_ROLLS, which is OFF by default, so with the flag unset this
# patch is behaviourally a no-op and EVERY process -- search, training, and the
# transition differential -- keeps the collapsed partition cascade bit-identically.
# When the flag is on, each chance branch emits one arm per distinct
# floor(max * r / 100) for r in 85..=100 at mass 1/16 (pre-merged on equal
# integers) instead of choosing a representative roll, and
# residual_lethality_threshold is not called at all.
#
# A runtime flag rather than a cargo feature, deliberately: one build serves both
# paths, so every collapsed-vs-enumerated comparison is single-variable.
#
# NOT adopted for the differential, and that reversal is the point. An earlier
# revision of this branch switched the differential to the enumerated path; review
# established that a differential running enumerated certifies a configuration
# production never takes, so the fidelity gate would stop measuring the shipping
# engine. Enumeration is instead an EXACT ORACLE for the collapsed path's masses:
# a wrong collapsed recipe stops being something review has to catch by reading and
# becomes a test that fails. Adopt-EVERYWHERE was separately measured and rejected
# on throughput. Decision: reports/c137_phase2_enumerate_decision.md. Prediction and
# sweeps: reports/c134_enumerate_rolls_oracle.md.
poke-engine-gen3-enumerate-damage-rolls.patch

# gen3 MOVE-TIME IMMOBILIZER ATTRIBUTION. Adds `Instruction::MoveImmobilized`
# (+ `ImmobilizeReason`, apply/reverse both no-ops) and pushes it into BOTH of
# gen3's move-time immobilizer branches -- the Attract-immobilized branch that
# `poke-engine-gen3-attract.patch` created, and the fully-paralyzed branch.
#
# THE DEFECT IT CLOSES: both branches were `incoming_instructions.clone()` with an
# EMPTY delta, so they were byte-identical to each other -- "the move did not
# happen" has no state representation -- and `combine_duplicate_instructions`
# MERGED them, along with any same-shaped miss or no-op. The renderer therefore
# could not say WHICH immobilizer fired: it refused the attracted case
# (`attract_empty_tail_ambiguous`) and guessed the paralyzed one from probability
# mass. The attract patch conceded it in its own comment: "both immobilized
# branches carry the same empty delta".
#
# HOW BIG THE REFUSED CLASS WAS -- the census, cited, because the code comments
# point here rather than restate it.
#
#   * Validation holdout, seeds 19,100,000-19,100,199, 200 games, 15,579 measured
#     boundaries, engine fingerprint 5fa147ffa325c887: `attract_empty_tail_ambiguous`
#     accounted for ALL THREE of the three `strict:lossy_render` refusals. 100% of
#     that window's lossy-render residue, 0.019% of its measured boundaries.
#     `reports/artifacts/c142_rumpfix_holdout_sweep.json` is the ONLY committed
#     sweep that breaks the 3 down by marker
#     (`strict:lossy_render_marker:attract_empty_tail_ambiguous: 3`). Its
#     `source_commit` does not resolve and its tree was dirty --
#     `reports/c142_rump_branch_adjudication.md` discloses that and why the numbers
#     still stand -- so the COUNT is taken from `c142_base_holdout_sweep.json`, same
#     window and fingerprint, `source_tree: clean`, `source_commit ce962c6e` which
#     resolves.
#   * Dev window, seeds 19,000,000-19,000,199, 15,503 measured boundaries: NONE.
#     The counter is absent entirely (`c142_{base,rumpfix}_dev_sweep.json`).
#   * The 3 is a property of the window, not of one build. Over the widest glob
#     available -- `reports/*.json` plus `reports/artifacts/*.json` selected on a
#     top-level `boundaries_measured`, 79 files, the corpus
#     `tests/test_boundary_verdict_partition.py` pins -- ALL 30 sweeps on the
#     validation-holdout window report `strict:lossy_render` at exactly 3, across 21
#     distinct engine fingerprints and 14 campaigns from c121 to c142, and ALL 29
#     dev-window sweeps do not carry the counter at all.
#   * It was also the LARGEST marker in the one census that ranked them:
#     `reports/c56_excluded_branch_census.json` puts it at 123 of the 218 markers on
#     excluded branches that would have matched (56.4%), against 39 / 29 / 27 for the
#     other three, and names it as the one to take next. That census is era-56 and is
#     NOT re-measured here.
#   * NOT a claim about the spent final holdout at 19,200,060, where
#     `c141_final_holdout_sweep.json` reports `strict:lossy_render` at 14 over 16,274
#     boundaries and no per-marker split exists.
#
# WITHDRAWN: earlier revisions of this entry, of the patch's own comment and of a
# crate test's doc comment said "~46% of the remaining search-fallback residue". No
# artifact carries that figure and no measurement above yields it: 3/3 is 100%,
# 3/15,579 is 0.019%, 123/218 is 56.4%, 90/366 is 24.6%. The glob, written into the
# sentence: `git grep -l 46%` over the WHOLE tree returns SEVEN files -- three
# unrelated `docs/checkpoint_trait_tracking_report*.html`, one report, and the three
# carrying this withdrawal (this file, the patch, and
# `gen3_confusion_event_renderer.rs`). Scoped to `reports/`, exactly ONE:
# `reports/c58_residue_partition.json`, where 46% means something else entirely --
# 157 of 341 rows "that no instrument fix can clear" -- and where the SAME FILE then
# retracts even that ("does not survive ... by arithmetic rather than by the evidence
# I cited"). That is the likeliest origin and it was never about this class. Recorded
# rather than quietly deleted: the figure was about to be frozen into engine source,
# where it would have outlived every report that could refute it. The commit that
# introduced the paralysis marker stated the figure had been removed; it had been
# removed from `events.rs` only, and survived in three other places.
#
# APPLY AND REVERSE ARE NO-OPS, so no mass moves and no leaf STATE moves. But the
# markers DO change the branch SET, deliberately, and an earlier revision of this
# entry denied it ("a pure marker, so it cannot move the leaf distribution"). The
# merge is what destroyed the attribution, so un-merging it IS the fix. Measured
# base-vs-head, side two attracted + paralyzed:
#
#   Tackle    base 2 branches (62.5 `[]` / 37.5 hit)
#             head 3 branches (50.0 Attract / 12.5 Paralysis / 37.5 hit)
#   Thunder   base 3 branches (73.75 `[]` / 18.375 / 7.875)
#             head 5 branches (50.0 Attract / 12.5 Paralysis / 11.25 `[]` / 18.375
#                              / 7.875)
#
# Total mass, leaf states and the union of the merged mass are all preserved
# (50.0 + 12.5 == 62.5; + 11.25 == 73.75). The branch count and per-branch masses
# are not. The residual `[]` on the Thunder fixture is the accuracy miss, which must
# stay UNMARKED because a miss is not an immobilization. Pinned by
# `the_markers_de_collapse_what_combine_duplicate_instructions_had_merged`.
#
# A useful consequence: the paralysis comment in `generate_instructions.rs` records
# that while both immobilized branches carried an empty delta the ORDER of the two
# immobilizers was invisible in the leaf distribution -- the reason the attract patch
# once called a misordering benign, before it turned out to corrupt the confusion
# counter. It is visible now: rolling paralysis first moves the Tackle split to
# 37.5/25.0 and the pin above goes red.
#
# THE LOSSY DOWNGRADE TO `|cant|..|par|` IS REJECTED, and the rejection does not
# rest on a frequency claim. An earlier revision cited "era-63, 3,344 attract
# slug-occurrences: pure `paralyzed` 38.4%, contaminated joints 61.6%". No artifact
# in this repo carries those numbers, and there is no era-63 artifact to carry them:
# `git grep -lE 'era[-_ ]63'` over the whole tree returns four files, two of them
# this withdrawal and two of them forward-looking notes about the era that will
# measure this fix, and `ls reports reports/artifacts` matches nothing era-63-shaped.
# Era shard reports are cluster-PVC aggregates that are not committed, as
# `src/pokezero/public_action_capture.py`'s own comment records of era 57.
# WITHDRAWN. Two grounds that ARE sourceable, neither depending on how often
# paralysis co-occurs:
#
#   * `src/pokezero/public_action_capture.py:74` keys public actions as
#     `cant:{reason or 'unknown'}`, so `cant:Attract` and `cant:par` are DIFFERENT
#     action ids downstream. Guessing one for the other is not a rounding error, it
#     is a different action.
#   * a wrong reason label can manufacture a false MATCH in the transition
#     differential, and `reports/c56_excluded_branch_census.json`
#     (`what_this_does_NOT_license`) rules that out as policy: "Admitting an
#     ambiguous branch to the comparison could manufacture false MATCHES, which is
#     worse than a false divergence because it hides a real difference." A downgrade
#     is exactly that trade, and it is worse than the refusal it replaced.
#
# Moot in any case now that BOTH immobilizers are marked: there is nothing left to
# downgrade, because there is nothing left to guess.
#
# LAST in the stack, and it must stay after `poke-engine-gen3-attract.patch`: it
# rewrites that patch's push site, and the surrounding text has since been
# changed by later patches (the OBLIVIOUS guard, the confusion-ladder rewrite
# that moved paralysis below Attract). Authored against the fully-patched tree.
#
# Touches FOUR files -- `src/instruction.rs`, `src/state.rs`,
# `src/gen3/generate_instructions.rs` and `tests/test_gen3.rs. Counted from the
# patch's own `+++` headers rather than recalled, and the same count corrected an
# earlier revision of this entry, which said THREE. The engine's unit-test modules
# live in `src/`, which is the `--lib` target; the three marker tests sit in
# `tests/test_gen3.rs` instead because that is the target CI runs.
#
# The comparison with the `rest-sleep-pending-refund` template is about WHICH files,
# not how many: that patch touches three (`src/state.rs`, `src/instruction.rs`,
# `poke-engine-py/src/lib.rs`) and the third is the one that matters here.
# `poke-engine-py/src/lib.rs` needs NO change, because this adds no
# `Pokemon`/`State` field for `PyPokemon` to construct. `PyInstruction` is an
# opaque wrapper whose only method is a `{:?}` repr, so the new variant crosses
# the binding with no arm to add (verified: the pyo3 crate compiles unchanged).
poke-engine-gen3-attract-marker.patch
# The Sleep Talk DOUBLE damage-dealt reset. Closes a `none_matched` refusal class
# ON THE IN-MEMORY FOLD PATH. Read the scope line before the numbers: this cannot
# close anything on the transition-differential corpus, and the reason is below.
#
# MEASURED by rust/pokezero-search/examples/gen3_sleeptalk_none_matched_census.rs on
# two builds whose vendored trees differ in EXACTLY ONE LINE, over 80 cells and
# 2,025 branches of the #1048 oracle's population carried on a LIVE `State`:
#   guard reverted, carry 137: 2,025 refused; shape_length 2,025; shape_structure 954
#   guarded,        carry 137:     0 refused; 1,840 attributed
#   EITHER build,   carry   0:     0 refused; 1,840 attributed   <- reachability control
# The zero-carry arm is what a DESERIALIZED boundary presents, and its identity
# across the two builds is what predicted the sweep null rather than explaining it
# afterwards. Artifacts reports/artifacts/c148_sleeptalk_double_reset_census_{base,gate}.json;
# sweeps reports/artifacts/c148_sleeptalk_double_reset_{base,gate}_{dev,holdout}_sweep.json,
# `counters` byte-identical on both windows. NO campaign-era fallback rate is claimed.
#
# WITHDRAWN, and recorded here because this file carried them: an earlier revision
# claimed `none_matched` 8,613 -> 0 over an 8,903-branch population, partitioning
# into 8,292 + 321 with 290 outside. No artifact ever supported those figures --
# `grep -rl none_matched reports/artifacts/*.json` returns 0 files -- and the 8,613
# counted AGGREGATE `none_matched`, not `shape_length`. The era-61 figure for
# `shape_length` (4,786 worlds, 33.3 %) is a source comment in events.rs from an
# uncommitted sweep; this change does not re-measure it and, per the reachability
# paragraph below, could not.
#
# `generate_instructions_from_move` opens by emitting the turn-start
# `damage_dealt` carry-over reset. The Sleep Talk block then calls
# `state.reverse_instructions(&incoming_instructions.instruction_list)` before
# recursing into the callee, which UNDOES that reset and restores the pre-reset
# carry-over into `state`; the callee's own call re-enters the same opening and
# pushes the SAME reset onto a list that already contains it. `reset_damage_dealt`
# reads `state` and only appends -- it never mutates the side -- so it cannot see
# the queued instruction.
#
# Two of the three sub-fields are non-idempotent under double emission and both
# fire: `ChangeDamageDealtDamage` is a DELTA (`0 - damage`), so applying it twice
# lands on `-damage` instead of 0, and `ToggleDamageDealtHitSubstitute` is a
# TOGGLE, so applying it twice restores the flag the reset meant to clear. Only
# `ChangeDamageDealtMoveCatagory` is an absolute set and is idempotent.
#
# Renderer consequence: `consume_move_prelude`
# (rust/pokezero-search/src/events.rs) eats EVERY leading damage-dealt
# instruction, so the tail it hands `identify_sleep_talk_called` starts after
# both, while that function's single regeneration emits ONE reset at the head.
# The divergence is therefore at INDEX 0 -- which is why the class always
# measured 0 `shape_branch_is_prefix_of_tail` and 0
# `shape_tail_is_prefix_of_branch`.
#
# The flag AND the carry are jointly necessary, which the census above shows on the
# shipping stack: the carry-0 arm is clean on BOTH builds, and
# `with_damage_dealt_tracking_off_no_reset_is_emitted` covers the flag. (An earlier
# revision quoted a factorial isolation of 245,284 `shape_length` + 109,836
# `shape_structure` over 11,520 states per arm. That was inherited from the 71-patch
# diagnosis, never re-measured, and is DROPPED rather than restated; the census
# figures above are measured on the stack that ships.)
# `state.use_damage_dealt` is set by `set_conditional_mechanics` whenever any of
# the twelve Pokemon knows Counter / Mirror Coat / Focus Punch, which is common
# in gen3 randbats and team-dependent.
#
# NOT purely a redundant instruction: the corrupted `-damage` is read by the
# opponent's COUNTER in the same turn (`gen3_fixed_damage_amount` returns
# `damage_dealt.damage * 2`).
#
# COUNTER IS THE ONLY CHANNEL THAT CAN EXIST, and the enumeration is exhaustive:
# gen3 has exactly THREE readers of `damage_dealt` -- everything else in the file
# is inside `reset_damage_dealt` or `set_damage_dealt`, which are the writers.
#   * COUNTER (generate_instructions.rs) gates only on
#     `move_category == Physical`, which the reset satisfies, and then returns
#     `damage * 2` UNGATED on sign: -274 against 0. This is the channel.
#   * MIRROR COAT (same function) gates on `move_category == Special`. The reset
#     writes Physical, and the category write is an absolute set and therefore the
#     one sub-field that IS idempotent under double emission -- so Mirror Coat
#     returns `Some(0)` under both engines. Immune.
#   * FOCUS PUNCH (choice_effects.rs:266) needs `damage > 0`; -137 and 0 both fail.
#     Its `!hit_substitute` clause cannot rescue the difference either: a corrupted
#     `hit_substitute == true` survives only when `set_damage_dealt` did not run --
#     it overwrites both fields absolutely -- and that is exactly the case where no
#     damage was dealt, so `damage > 0` is already false. Immune on both fields.
# That reader exhaustion is a SOURCE argument and was independently confirmed by
# review. An earlier revision paired it with measured counts -- 70 differing cells of
# 4,368, 26 triples, 18 full-HP; and a 5,184-cell decomposition reporting 594
# identical / 4,590 differing once `damage_dealt` was included. Those came from an
# uncommitted diagnosis run and are WITHDRAWN, not restated. What ships instead is a
# digest: the census records `(cell, serialized end state) -> mass` in integer
# micro-percent and hashes the whole map, and all four arms return the same digest
# over 1,899 distinct end states. Note what that does and does not say. Because
# `Side::serialize` omits `damage_dealt`, the projection EXCLUDES the field being
# repaired -- it says the observable outcome distribution does not move, NOT that the
# corruption is harmless. On this population Counter's `damage * 2` is -274 under the
# defect and 0 under the guard and neither emits a damage event, so both land on the
# same serialized state by different routes. A population that separates them is not
# committed.
#
# REACHABILITY, and it bounds every claim above. An earlier revision of this comment
# said the differential "reaches the engine only through `branch_events`". THAT WAS A
# FALSE TOTALITY CLAIM in a change whose whole purpose is retiring one, and it was
# wrong: `branch_events` is one of THREE entry points. The conclusion survives, but
# on a mechanism that revision never cited. The enumeration, from
# `grep -n 'poke_engine\.\|pokezero_search\.' scripts/engine_transition_differential.py`:
#
#  1. `:2057` `pokezero_search.branch_events(state.to_string(), ...)`. SERIALIZES
#     first, so `State::deserialize` runs. `Side::serialize`
#     (third_party/poke-engine-src/src/state.rs:1292) formats 29 fields and
#     `damage_dealt` is not one of them, and `Side::deserialize` (:1394) hardcodes
#     `damage_dealt: DamageDealt::default()`. Carry presented: ZERO.
#  2. `:2304` `poke_engine.generate_instructions(state, ...)` on the LIVE Python
#     `State` -- `state`, not `state.to_string()` -- built by
#     `build_poke_engine_state` (`src/pokezero/poke_engine_adapter.py:298`) through
#     the pyo3 constructors, which never call `from_string`. So `State::deserialize`
#     is NOT involved on this route, and it does reach the guarded function:
#     `poke-engine-py/src/lib.rs:1067` -> `:1092`
#     `generate_instructions_from_move_pair`. The carry is zeroed anyway, by a
#     DIFFERENT mechanism: the `PySide -> Side` conversion hardcodes
#     `damage_dealt: Default::default()` at `poke-engine-py/src/lib.rs:263`, and
#     `PyState -> State` sets `use_damage_dealt: false` at `:84` before calling
#     `state.set_conditional_mechanics()` at `:86`. Carry presented: ZERO.
#  3. `:842` and `:2075` `poke_engine.calculate_damage(...)` ->
#     `poke-engine-py/src/lib.rs:1099` -> `calculate_both_damage_rolls`
#     (`src/gen3/generate_instructions.rs:6437`) -> `calculate_damage_rolls`. This
#     route never calls `generate_instructions_from_move` at all, so the guarded
#     block is not on it. (`:841` feeds it a `State.from_string` state, i.e. route 1's
#     zeroing as well.)
#
# `DamageDealt::default()` is `{damage: 0, move_category: Physical, hit_substitute:
# false}` (state.rs:586), and all three of `reset_damage_dealt`'s guards test against
# exactly those values -- so on a zero carry it emits NOTHING, and emitting nothing
# twice is emitting nothing. Both zeroing routes still run
# `set_conditional_mechanics`, so the FLAG is set from movesets while the VALUE is
# zero. THE SWEEP CORPUS THEREFORE CANNOT OBSERVE THIS FIX ON ANY OF ITS THREE ENTRY
# POINTS. `env_step` is a fourth consumer outside the differential and is zeroed by
# route 1's mechanism, and additionally returns `post_state: state.serialize()`, so
# the carry cannot survive between calls either. Only the in-memory tree fold
# (`model.rs` / `tree.rs`, apply/reverse on a live `State`) can reach it, at depth
# >= 2.
